newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to open pension review in 1997 - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy to open pension review in 1997 - Prodi.

text.p: The Italian government will initiate a review of last year's pension reform deal in 1997 and introduce changes to the system in 1998, Prime Minister Romano Prodi told reporters.
Under the terms of the original deal, the review was not due to begin until 1998 and union leaders have fiercely rejected suggestions that the revision should be brought forward.

"We will start talks with all the social partners, from unions to companies, from the church to young people...that way we will have the reform ready for 1998," Prodi said, adding that this remained within the spirit of the 1995 deal.
Analysts have criticised the pension reform, enacted by the then prime minister Lamberto Dini, for being too slow moving in eradicating generous early retirement packages.

Commentators have said Italy needs to restructure its pensions spending if it is to balance its books and get the ratio between the state deficit and gross domestic product below the three percent level.
However an effective revision will be hard to achieve in the current political climate.
The hardline Communist Refoundation, which guarantees the centre-left government's majority in the lower house of parliament, has repeatedly rejected calls for pension reform.
Italy's three main unions, more than half of whose members are pensioners, are also expected to put up a tough fight against pension changes. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
